findings.text: Provides a predicate that reports whether direct input output on an inode has fully completed by checking for a zero outstanding count.

Remap request validation requires block aligned start offsets, rejects arithmetic wrap of ranges, limits the source extent to current source size, applies destination write limits, normalizes length to block granularity with end of file rounding, forbids overlapping ranges within one file, and permits a shortened length only when REMAP_FILE_CAN_SHORTEN allows it, using EINVAL for validation failures; REMAP_FILE_DEDUP selects deduplication mode.
For deduplication the same validation additionally requires both source and destination ranges to fall entirely inside their respective current file sizes.

Write limit handling caps length by RLIMIT_FSIZE with a size exceeded signal when already at the limit, selects between superblock maximum and legacy small file ceiling based on O_LARGEFILE, rejects positions beyond the maximum with EFBIG, and trims the request to the remaining allowance.

Remap length handling accepts already aligned lengths, otherwise trims a trailing partial block only when the destination range reaches beyond destination size, commits the trimmed value when REMAP_FILE_CAN_SHORTEN is present, and otherwise fails with EBADE for REMAP_FILE_DEDUP and EINVAL for copy.

Deduplication equality checking advances through the extent in page bounded steps, obtains one cached folio per side per step, locks the pair, revalidates currency and file association after locking, transiently maps both with cache maintenance before byte comparison, releases all resources each step, stops on first difference or invalidation, and reports the outcome through an output flag with EINVAL as the initial failure status.

Paired folio locking acquires in increasing index order and locks only once when both inputs are the same folio, while paired unlocking releases symmetrically with a single release in the shared case.

Dentry population accounting uses a six slot record holding total count, unused count, age limit, wanted pages, unused negative count and a reserved slot, with live totals kept in per processor counters plus a policy control and a global instance carrying an initial age.
Oversize dentry names live in a trailing variable buffer preceded by a reference count and a deferred free header with strong alignment, distinct from short names stored directly inside the dentry.
Completion chaining uses a node with a link to the next node and an embedded completion object.
Submount probe state pairs a mount reference with a numeric found indicator.
Shrink collection state holds a start dentry that is skipped, a shared result slot usable as a count or as a victim pointer, and a private dispose list.
Tree walk control defines four outcomes for continuing descent, quitting entirely, quitting without retry, and skipping a subtree.

Pressure scaling computes a proportional value from a numerator and denominator that both default to 100 and are writable with lower bounds, while dentry state is read only and negative policy is a bounded boolean; filesystem and memory control tables publish these under defined names and both tables are registered during early initialization.

Live dentry totals are obtained by summing per processor counters across all possible processors with clamping at zero, and a state handler refreshes the global record from those sums before delegating to a generic bounded vector handler.
In lookup hash width is 10 with a table of 1024 buckets.
Well known dentry names are empty with length 0, slash with length 1 and double dot with length 2, and the initial dentry age limit is 45.

Published control names are dentry-state and dentry-negative under filesystem controls plus vfs_cache_pressure and vfs_cache_pressure_denom under memory controls, with mode 0444 for state and 0644 for the tunables, and pressure numerator and denominator both default to 100.

Name snapshot acquisition runs under read side critical section with sequence retry, takes an inline copy for short names and a live counted reference for external names with retry if the target is being freed, and validates the sequence before release of the critical section; release drops the external reference and defers free when last.
Dontcache marking holds the inode lock while iterating all aliases and takes each alias lock briefly to set DCACHE_DONTCACHE, then records I_DONTCACHE on the inode before releasing.

Alias discovery holds the inode lock during search; directory case returns first alias with a reference, non directory cases prefer hashed entries or any grabbable alias with special handling for DCACHE_NORCU, with a read variant that checks I_FREEING and emptiness under the same inode lock.

Dentry least recently used isolation and shrink movement manipulate DCACHE_LRU_LIST and DCACHE_SHRINK_LIST membership under appropriate locks, adjust per processor unused and negative tallies, and reclamation paths acquire dentry lock by trylock because list lock to dentry lock order is inverted.

Per dentry reclaim decision skips entries whose lock is contended, detaches entries with active references, gives DCACHE_REFERENCED idle entries another rotation with flag cleared, and otherwise moves unreferenced idle entries to a private freeable list.

Subtree shrink walk skips the start node, moves dead or zero reference entries to a dispose list while counting, exits early once progress exists with scheduling friendliness, and has variants that clear DCACHE_PERSISTENT with reference drop or capture an unmovable victim under extended read protection.
Submount detection walks descendants under mount read protection and reports true if any mountpoint dentry corresponds to a live mount without MNT_SYNC_UMOUNT.

Reclamation entry points provide per superblock shrink walk with callback driven collection followed by list disposal, a looping drain in batches of 1024 until the per superblock least recently used count reaches zero, and an alias pruning pass that moves reclaimable aliases off their inode to a private list for disposal.

Cursor allocation creates an anonymous dentry marked with DCACHE_DENTRY_CURSOR and DCACHE_NORCU with a referenced parent; external name teardown frees the name then the dentry cache object; unmount validation warns on busy non root entries; submount search returns the first mountpoint encountered with a reference.

Remap must reject wrapped offsets, misaligned starts, out of file source ranges, overlapped same file copies and unpermitted shortening to avoid corruption or silent truncation; write limit path must signal and cap rather than overflow.

Deduplication comparison must revalidate currency and mapping after locking to avoid comparing stale or invalidated pages, must order pair locks to avoid deadlock, and must always release mappings locks and references even on mismatch.

Name snapshots must retry on concurrent rename and on zero counted external names to avoid use after free; alias grabs must not acquire zero reference non read copy update entries; least recently used callbacks must use trylock and respect shrink list isolation to avoid deadlock and list corruption.
Dentry cache access goes through a runtime constant pointer frozen after initialization, with hash shift and primary table similarly frozen for the lifetime of the system.
